chunks: And everything in this book that is narrated from Muhammad ibn Al-Fayd Al-Taymi has been transmitted by me from my father - may Allah be pleased with him - from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Dawud ibn Ishaq Al-Haddha', from Muhammad ibn Al-Fayd Al-Taymi.

key_terms.أَبِي: My father, referring to the author's father
key_terms.أَحْمَدُ بْنُ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, a narrator in the chain
key_terms.أَحْمَدُ بْنُ إِدْرِيسَ: Ahmad ibn Idris, a narrator in the chain
key_terms.دَاوُدُ بْنُ إِسْحَاقَ الْحَذَّاءِ: Dawud ibn Ishaq Al-Haddha', a narrator in the chain
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: May Allah be pleased with him
key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْفَيْضِ التَّيْمِيُّ: Muhammad ibn Al-Fayd Al-Taymi, a narrator

ai.seo_question: How is the transmission chain for Muhammad ibn Al-Fayd Al-Taymi verified in this text?
ai.summary: This passage highlights Shaykh al-Saduq’s meticulous approach to verifying the isnad (transmission chain) of Muhammad ibn Al-Fayd Al-Taymi, a key narrator in Shia hadith literature. By tracing the chain back to his own father (Abu Ja'far), al-Saduq establishes a direct and reliable link, reinforcing the authenticity of the narrations in *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih*. This emphasis on lineage and direct transmission underscores the Shia scholarly tradition of prioritizing strong, unbroken chains to ensure the integrity of religious teachings.
